nodes.label: Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement:
**Lemma 3.1.** There are odd smooth $1$-periodic functions $F_h$, $0<h\le1$, with zero-mean primitives $P_h$, such that $$F_h'(0)=1,\qquad -Ch\le F_h'\le1,\qquad
 \left\lVert F_h\right\rVert_\infty\le Ch,\qquad
 \left\lVert\partial_s^jF_h\right\rVert_\infty\le C_jh^{1-j}\quad(j\ge2).$$

nodes.label: Proposition 8.1
nodes.statement: **Proposition 8.1.** The data $U_j(0)$ converge in every $C^{m,1/2}$ to an odd divergence-free field $u_0$. In particular, $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Let $u$ be the maximal smooth solution of the Euler equations from $u_0$, with maximal time $T_*>0$, supplied by Section 1. Then $T_*\ge T_\infty$ and, for every $T<T_\infty$ and integer $m\ge0$, $U_j\to u$ in $C([0,T];C^{m,1/2})$. The solution is smooth and odd on $[0,T_\infty)\times\mathbb T^3$.
nodes.boundary: A result as the authors number it. Its links to the Lean were made with AI for Proof Reader and have not been reviewed by the authors.

nodes.label: Proposition 8.2
nodes.statement: **Proposition 8.2.** The solution has bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$, and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\longrightarrow\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$.
nodes.boundary: A result as the authors number it. Its links to the Lean were made with AI for Proof Reader and have not been reviewed by the authors.

nodes.label: Proposition 8.4
nodes.statement: **Proposition 8.4.** For every compact $K\subset\mathbb T^3\setminus\{0\}$ and every integer $m\ge0$, both $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge in $C^m(K)$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$.

nodes.label: Remark 1.2
nodes.statement: **Remark 1.2.** The solution in Theorem 1.1 may be chosen so that it extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from the origin. A proof is given in the auxiliary note \[[31](#cite-TerminalSmoothness)\].
